original.title: The Foucault Effect: Studies in Governmentality
original.note: Book checked in Open Library (/works/OL19850964W, first published 1991). ISBN is one edition's; cite the edition you read.

core_idea: Modern government works less by command than by shaping how people conduct themselves. It relies on rationalities (ways of thinking about rule) and technologies (statistics, audits, programmes) that make populations governable.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do development programmes, NGOs or policies shape people's self-conduct?
How do audits, indicators or rankings govern institutions?
Typical data: discourse and document analysis, ethnography.
common_mistakes: Using governmentality as a synonym for government.
Describing technologies without the rationality behind them.
Ignoring resistance and how people use programmes.
